children: Canadian firms and households are building in higher inflation expectations, and that leaves the Bank of Canada little choice but to raise rates, says Royce Mendes, head of macro strategy at Desjardins Group. "Central bankers view anchored longer-term inflation expectations as key to keep price growth near the target," says Mendes, noting the BOC sets policy to achieve and maintain 2% CPI. Core inflation is a tad below the 2% target, and that gives the BOC "more scope for a dovish set of communications" to accompany the rate rise, Mendes says. Inflation expectations in Canada are on the upswing due to higher fuel costs. (paul.vieira@wsj.com; @paulvieira)
